children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Indian equities ended October on a positive note after two consecutive months of losses, with the benchmark indices gaining on Friday, led by information technology, pharmaceutical and select heavyweight stocks. The recovery, however, was uneven, with midcap and smallcap stocks ending the month with losses amid lingering concerns over elevated crude oil prices and uncertainty surrounding the AI investment theme.

The Nifty reclaimed the 23,000 mark on Friday, gaining 116.35 points, or 0.51%, to close at 23,053.10. The Sensex rose 308.49 points, or 0.42%, to settle at 74,459.53. For October, the Sensex gained 2.7%, while the Nifty advanced nearly 2%. The benchmarks had declined 5.82% and 6.06%, respectively, in September, following losses of 1.46% and 1.24% in August.

In July, the Sensex and Nifty had gained 2.11% and 2.17%, respectively. The Nifty Midcap 150 declined 3.7% in October, while the Nifty Smallcap index fell 5.5%. "Indian equity markets have had a volatile October, with global uncertainties, elevated crude prices, continued FII selling and mixed corporate earnings keeping sentiment cautious," said Ankur Punj, managing director, Equirus Wealth.

While domestic institutional flows have provided support, the market is yet to demonstrate a convincing and sustainable recovery, he said. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) net bought equities worth 3,598 crore on Friday, taking their total net sales in October to 45,161 crore. Domestic institutional investors, meanwhile, were net sellers of equities worth 817.51 crore, taking their cumulative net purchases during the month to 62,220 crore.

Both benchmark indices gained nearly 2% during the week, recovering from the sharp selling pressure seen earlier in October. The broader market, however, remained under pressure on Friday. The Nifty Midcap 150 fell 0.8%, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 declined 1.8%. For the week, the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 2.5% and 4%, respectively.

Among sectoral indices, IT was the biggest gainer on Friday, rising 2.5%, followed by pharma, which advanced 1.7%. Consumer durables, energy and media declined more than 1% each. Auto, banking, PSU banks and FMCG stocks also ended lower. The rupee snapped its two-session losing streak, closing at 94.95 against the US dollar compared with Thursday's close of 95.25. Brent crude oil prices remained elevated, crossing $116 a barrel. Prices have risen almost 14% in October.

Monarch Networth Capital is turning constructive on Indian equities in the near term. "The worst of the FII selling pressure appears behind us, and as dollar weakness accelerates, we expect fresh capital flows into Indian markets," said Gaurav Bhandari, CEO, Monarch Networth Capital. He advised investors to use interim declines to build positions in quality stocks across financials, infrastructure and domestic consumption themes.

title: Not Quite an Octoberfest, but D-St Makes a Recovery
